issues: [security][medium confidence, disclosed-not-fixed] The `[[ ! -e "$d" && ! -L "$d" ]]` leg returns SUCCESS (0) when the parent is merely inaccessible rather than absent, reproducing one directory level up the exact 'cannot judge == not a link' conflation this round set out to eliminate. Measured: grandparent chmod 000 -> exit 0 in both old and new hooks. Not a regression, and the real write also fails with EACCES in that window (target byte-identical), so no live bypass exists. Explicitly disclosed in both the function comment and INVARIANTS.md, and assigned to F69-class follow-up — therefore per this round's scope it is NOT a fail reason. It is the single reason security is 8 rather than 9.

[security][low confidence] Residual TOCTOU on the disclosed leg: the guard's allow and the kernel's refusal are two separate moments, so a concurrent process that restores permissions between them could in principle convert the fail-open into a real write. Requires an already-running attacker process with chmod rights inside the repo; noted for completeness, not actionable this round.

[code_quality][high confidence] The inline comment on that leg asserts a cause the predicate cannot establish — '부모 디렉터리 자체가 없다 — 신규 경로 스캐폴딩' is stated as fact when `! -e && ! -L` cannot distinguish absence from EACCES. The function-level comment six lines above does disclose the limit, so the file is not self-contradictory, but the leg comment is exactly the overconfident-annotation pattern lessons.md flagged in the two preceding rounds.

[code_quality][high confidence] `canon_file()` retains a structurally identical silent fail-open: `d=$(cd "$d" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || { printf '%s' "$p"; return 0; }` returns success on an unenterable directory. It runs BEFORE resolve_file_symlink, so the immediate-parent case is covered by the new return-code contract, but the same 'undecidable -> success' shape survives one function away and is the mechanism behind the grandparent leg.

[code_quality][low] Each hop runs `cd "$d"` twice — once as the access probe, once inside the readlink command substitution. Harmless (max ~20 subshells; measured ~210ms for a 12-hop chain) but redundant.

[error][medium confidence] One deny message covers two materially different causes (depth cap exhausted vs. access denied) and prints the partially-resolved intermediate path (`.../sub/inner`) rather than the path the caller actually asked to write (`alias.json`). A caller cannot tell from the message which failure occurred or which of their files triggered it.

[test][medium confidence] No test pins the documented grandparent limit. Because the limit is now an explicit written promise about behavior, an untested promise can drift silently in either direction — a test asserting today's exit 0 would both fix the documentation to reality and turn red the day someone closes it.

[test][medium confidence] The 9/10/11/12-hop boundary tests assert exit code only, and this round measured that two different mechanisms both produce exit 2 (real SC-4 firing for fully-resolved chains, depth-cap fail-closed beyond it). If resolution broke entirely, all four cases would stay green for the wrong reason; only the 1-hop test (test 261) indirectly confirms that resolution actually happened. This is the same blind spot class that let the 11th-round defect survive its own test.

[process][low confidence] The 11th and 12th rounds' defects are recorded in progress/lessons.md but not in evals/calibration/false-positives.json. Both rounds ended in fail, so nothing escaped a pass verdict and the omission is defensible under the F37 definition of an escaped defect — reported for coverage, no action proposed.

verdict_rationale: The one defect this round was asked to close is closed, and closed for a defensible reason rather than by accident — verified by feeding identical input to the parent and HEAD hooks rather than by trusting the implementer's self-report. The suite is green with the new test proven non-vacuous. Most significantly for a repository whose recurring failure mode across F52/F63/F65/F68 has been documentation that claims more safety than the code delivers, this commit's documentation is now measurably not stronger than its code: it withdraws a claim that became false, states a scope widening that is real, and names an unclosed leg that measurement confirms is genuinely unclosed. A limitation disclosed and scoped out is not a fail reason. min-of-5 is 7 against a threshold of 7, and security is 8 against a critical floor of 7, so the gate opens — but it opens at the threshold, and the residual grandparent leg plus the two testing blind spots above are the agenda for F69.
